title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a law that establishes strict standards for testing, safety, and transparency in AI research to make sure new systems are trustworthy. It creates oversight mechanisms and funding requirements that hold researchers accountable and encourage the development of AI that performs reliably and safely before it is deployed.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to prevent misleading or deceptive AI-generated content from harming consumers. It establishes rules and penalties for companies that provide AI tools that misinform or deceive users, ensuring greater transparency and accountability.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a proposed law that aims to strengthen the safety and security of advanced AI systems. It intends to set up rules and protocols to ensure AI is used responsibly and to protect against potential risks and vulnerabilities.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is designed to protect the integrity of elections by limiting the use of AI-generated misinformation and deceptive content that could influence voters. It proposes regulations on AI in political campaigns and requires transparency and accountability to keep elections fair and reliable.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a federal task force to improve the security of artificial intelligence systems across the United States. It aims to coordinate efforts among government agencies, industry partners, and researchers to identify vulnerabilities and develop protective measures for AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to establish comprehensive guidelines and oversight to ensure AI technologies are developed, deployed, and monitored in a way that protects public safety, privacy, and national security. It aims to create a framework for risk assessment, transparency, and accountability among AI developers and users, while setting standards for security measures and compliance enforcement.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 is a law that establishes rules and oversight for the design, deployment, and operation of AI-powered physical systems such as robots, autonomous vehicles, and drones. It aims to ensure safety, accountability, and coordination among manufacturers, regulators, and users, while promoting responsible innovation and protecting public interests.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The proposed amendment to the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 would require that any political advertisement containing images or video footage generated by artificial intelligence must include a clear statement indicating that AI was used. This measure aims to increase transparency and accountability in political advertising by making the use of generative AI in campaign content publicly known.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to prevent AI-generated misinformation from influencing electoral processes. It introduces safeguards and penalties for using AI to create deceptive content that could sway voters.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes mandatory oversight for AI systems that can autonomously modify their own code or behavior. It requires developers to implement continuous monitoring, regular reporting, and safety verification to ensure such systems operate within legal and ethical boundaries.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act proposes legislative measures to curb the development and deployment of autonomous artificial intelligence systems that pose significant risks to public safety and security. It aims to establish stringent oversight, accountability frameworks, and enforcement mechanisms to prevent the use of potentially malicious or uncontrolled AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act is a proposed law that would temporarily halt the building and operation of large AI data centers. This moratorium is intended to address concerns over energy consumption, environmental impact, and social implications associated with the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act establishes a dedicated board to investigate cybersecurity incidents that involve artificial intelligence systems. The board will oversee investigations, recommend safeguards, and provide guidance to protect against AI‑driven cyber threats.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is a proposed law that aims to shape the development and deployment of AI so that it benefits U.S. citizens. It seeks to ensure that AI technologies are safe, fair, and accessible, helping Americans gain from advancements while protecting their interests.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a proposed law that would require Chinese companies and government bodies to disclose detailed information about their artificial intelligence systems and capabilities. This reporting would help regulators track AI development, promote transparency, and address potential security and ethical concerns.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 bars artificial intelligence from independently diagnosing or treating patients without a licensed human doctor’s oversight. The law requires all AI‑driven health tools to operate only under direct supervision of qualified medical professionals.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The bill creates a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the President’s Executive Office, tasked with monitoring and mitigating risks from AI and other emerging technologies. It also outlines additional responsibilities and powers for the office to address related national security and policy challenges.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution establishes a Select Committee dedicated to overseeing and guiding artificial intelligence policy. The committee will examine AI’s impacts, recommend regulations, and ensure responsible development.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for thoroughly assessing the risks of AI systems before they are deployed. It aims to safeguard public safety, privacy, and national security by setting standards and accountability for AI developers and users.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed federal law aimed at establishing clear standards and safeguards for the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems. It seeks to protect public safety, privacy, and fairness by requiring transparency, accountability, and rigorous risk assessments for AI applications across industries.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes regulations to assess and mitigate the environmental effects of AI technologies, including power consumption, heat generation, and electronic waste. It requires companies to report energy use, adopt greener data‑center practices, and incentivize the development of more sustainable AI systems.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students, teachers, and schools with the knowledge and tools needed to understand and responsibly use artificial intelligence. It establishes a framework for curriculum development, professional training, and assessment standards to prepare the next generation for an AI‑driven world.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to strengthen the safety and reliability of AI systems by establishing rigorous research standards and promoting transparency. It aims to fund thorough testing, create oversight mechanisms, and encourage collaboration between academia, industry, and regulators to ensure AI technologies are trustworthy and aligned with public values.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, via the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to launch a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to defend critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. It also includes additional measures aimed at strengthening national cyber defense capabilities.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that requires schools to teach students about artificial intelligence and how to use it responsibly. It sets up standards, resources, and training so students and teachers are prepared for a future where AI is common.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that sets rules for how artificial intelligence can be used in handling veterans’ claims. It aims to make the AI systems fair, transparent and accountable so veterans are protected from bias or mistakes in automated decisions.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose the use of artificial intelligence in its services and decision‑making processes. It mandates that veterans receive clear information about how AI systems influence care, benefits, and eligibility, and establishes oversight to ensure ethical and fair AI deployment.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The act aims to increase public understanding of artificial intelligence through a nationwide educational and awareness campaign. It seeks to promote transparency, address societal concerns, and empower citizens to make informed decisions about AI technology.
